content_voiceover: Now a concrete, high-yield example of protein polymorphism, the RhD negative null phenotype. On chromosome one, RHD and RHCE sit as two homologous genes in tandem, flanked by Rh box sequences, with TMEM50A in between. The most common mechanism for RhD negative status isn't a point mutation, it's a complete deletion of the RHD gene, mediated by homologous recombination between those flanking Rh boxes. So a truly RhD negative person has no RHD gene at all, they only retain RHCE, which still produces the RhCcEe protein, just no D antigen whatsoever. This is a true null phenotype, not a weak or altered antigen. The number that matters most for boards is the striking racial difference in prevalence, Rh negative is only about zero point three percent in Taiwan, compared to about fifteen percent in Caucasians. That's roughly a fifty-fold difference, and it has real clinical implications for how often Rh negative blood needs to be stocked and how Rh alloimmunization risk is counseled across different populations.
keypoints: RHD and RHCE are tandem homologous genes on chromosome 1, flanked by Rh boxes
RhD negative usually = complete RHD gene deletion via Rh box recombination, a true null
Only RHCE remains, still making RhCcEe protein, just no D antigen
Taiwan Rh negative ~0.3% versus Caucasian ~15%, about a 50-fold difference
